model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: Model identity is the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, read from the session environment (claude-opus-5[1m], Opus 5 with 1M context). The agent definition's template text names claude-fable-5; that template value was deliberately not used, because it would assert an evaluator identity this run did not have.

issues_detected.description: All fifteen entries under creators are typed principal_investigator, while the record's own notes mark only two of them as such: 'Co-principal investigator of the Bridge2AI-Voice project' appears on Yael Bensoussan and Olivier Elemento and on no other entry. The remaining thirteen (Sigaras, Rameau, Powell, Bahr, Siu, Payne, Dorr, Belisle-Pipon, Ravitsky, Ghosh, Rudzicz, Lerner-Ellis, Bolser) carry a role the record does not evidence, flattening site leads, technical leads and ethicists into one role.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reserve principal_investigator for the two contributors the sources name as co-PIs and re-type the rest to the role the sources support (site investigator, co-investigator, technical lead), or state in notes that the slot is used as a generic contributor role

issues_detected.description: Which demographic fields survive de-identification cannot be settled from the record. sensitive_elements asserts the dataset 'includes race and ethnic origin information' and 'includes sexual orientation information', while is_deidentified.identifiers_removed states that 'select geographic and demographic identifiers and information about household composition or cultural identity' and 'non-identifying but highly sensitive fields such as household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences' were removed. A user planning a fairness analysis cannot tell whether race, ethnicity and sexual orientation are in the released phenotype tables.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the demographic variables retained in the released phenotype tables and those removed, so that sensitive_elements and is_deidentified describe the same release

issues_detected.description: No publisher slot is populated. PhysioNet is identified unambiguously in five other places (page URL, the citation string, maintainers, third_party_sharing 'through the PhysioNet data publishing platform', and data_governance.stewardship_roles), and the Health Data Nexus is identified as the publisher of the superseded release, so a human reader loses nothing; a metadata harvester reading the publisher slot gets nothing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate publisher with PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, matching the platform already named in citation and maintainers

issues_detected.description: No software_and_tools slot exists, and no feature-extraction library carries a version. The processing tools are named with their parameters inside preprocessing_strategies (sparc, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, ppgs, Whisper Large) and their repositories appear in external_resources (sensein/b2aiprep, sensein/senselab), but only 'Whisper Large' and 'Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0' are pinned at all. Feature values from openSMILE and Praat are version-dependent, so the released Parquet features cannot be reproduced from what is recorded.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add software_and_tools naming b2aiprep, senselab, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, sparc and ppgs with the versions or release tags used to produce this release

issues_detected.description: keywords carries four single-word entries (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) against a record that names five disease cohort categories, eight derived feature families, BIDS, REDCap, ICD-10, PhysioNet, Synapse and four acoustic modalities. Searchable terms the record itself asserts (speech, cough, respiratory, spectrogram, MFCC, phonetic posteriorgram, machine learning, PhysioNet, BIDS, Parkinson, dysphonia) are absent from the keyword set.
issues_detected.recommendation: Expand keywords to at least a dozen terms drawn from the record's own content: modality, derived feature family, disease cohort, standard and hosting platform

issues_detected.description: confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, asserting no data protected by legal privilege or doctor-patient confidentiality, while the same entry's source_caveats records that 'the underlying data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality, which must be asserted against compulsory legal demands such as court orders and subpoenas'. The two claims are reconcilable (the certificate covers the identifiable source data held at sites, not the released features), but the record leaves the reconciliation to the reader.
issues_detected.recommendation: State in confidentiality_details that the Certificate of Confidentiality attaches to the identifiable source data retained at collecting institutions rather than to the released feature set

issues_detected.description: updates.frequency is recorded as 'Semi-annual (twice a year)', while distribution_dates lists six releases between the end of November 2024 and 1 May 2026: 1.0, 1.1 (17 January 2025), 2.0.0 (16 April 2025), 2.0.1 (18 August 2025), 3.0.0 (16 December 2025) and 3.1.0 (1 May 2026). The observed cadence is closer to quarterly, so the stated frequency understates the release rate a reuser should plan for.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the frequency the release history shows, or say that semi-annual is the planned cadence and that interim corrective releases have been more frequent

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes states 'The data were collected over a period of 12 months' with no start or end date, and its own source_caveats records the conflict with an IRB protocol describing a four-year phased study with pilot collection begun in November 2023 and ongoing in November 2024. A twelve-month window is also hard to reconcile with six releases spanning eighteen months and 833 participants across five sites. The record names the conflict and declines to resolve it, which is the right disclosure, but leaves the reuser without a dated collection window.
issues_detected.recommendation: Give the collection window for the participants in this release as calendar dates, even approximate ones, rather than a bare duration

issues_detected.description: The audio recording entry under instances carries no counts, so the only structured count in the record is 833 participants. The recording-level figures exist but sit in the trailing source_caveats prose (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram files for version 3.1.0, against approximately 61,937 voice-derived recordings in the project documentation for version 3.0), where no structured consumer will read them.
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the per-feature recording counts into the audio recording instance entry, keeping the caveat that the sources disagree on a single recording total

issues_detected.description: The top-level license names only 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License', which governs the feature-only release, while distribution_formats includes a WAV component whose access is governed by a Data Access Request Form, a Data Use Agreement, DACO review and an institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement. One licence string is carried for a two-tier release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Say in license_terms that the named licence governs the registered-access feature release and that the controlled-access audio is governed by the DUA and DTUA instead

issues_detected.description: RRID:SCR_007345 is well formed and is the correct Research Resource Identifier for PhysioNet, but it sits inside the free-text citation string rather than an identifier slot, so it is not machine-readable. It also identifies the hosting platform rather than the dataset, which is the conventional use in a PhysioNet citation but is worth stating.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the RRID in the citation as published and, if a resource identifier for the platform is wanted structurally, record it in a dedicated slot with a note that it identifies PhysioNet

semantic_insights: Identifier discipline is correct and unusually explicit: id and doi carry the version-specific PhysioNet DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 for version 3.1.0, version_access.latest_version_doi carries the version-agnostic 10.13026/37yb-1t42, version_details enumerates the per-version DOIs, and source_caveats states the choice as a referent decision rather than leaving it implicit.

Every DOI prefix in the record is plausible for the registrar it is attributed to: 10.13026 for the PhysioNet releases and the related pediatric dataset, 10.5281 for the two Zenodo software archives, and 10.57764 for the Health Data Nexus release at the University of Toronto.

The five Element 4 consistency expectations all pass. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and irb_approval, ethics_review_board and three ethical_reviews entries are populated; is_deidentified names HIPAA Safe Harbor and enumerates the identifier set removed; informed_consent carries type, scope, documentation and withdrawal; participant_privacy assesses re-identification risk explicitly rather than asserting safety.

The re-identification assessment is semantically appropriate for the data type rather than generic: it concedes that k-anonymisation with k of 2 or more is not achieved, states that a voice is unique to its speaker so re-identification cannot be excluded, and derives the two-tier access model from that finding, which is why the raw audio is withheld from the registered-access release.

Preprocessing is documented at parameter level rather than by tool name alone: 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter, a 25 ms window with 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT, sixty MFCCs and 60-bin Mel spectrograms, articulatory traces at 50 Hz and phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 acoustic units at 100 Hz. This is enough for a reuser to interpret the released Parquet columns, though not to reproduce them without library versions.

known_biases uses four distinct schema enum values (representation_bias, selection_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias), each with a description grounded in a specific collection fact and, for representation bias, a stated mitigation. The measurement bias entry connects device and site variation to disease cohort, which is the confound that matters most for a voice classifier.

The NIH award identifiers are well formed for the agency named: OT2OD032720 matches the Other Transaction activity code and Office of the Director institute pattern, and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 is a valid full award number with a supplement suffix. source_caveats lists the competing renderings found across the sources and explicitly declines the malformed footer string '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2'.

The record repeatedly ranks conflicting sources rather than silently choosing: on the free-speech transcripts it prefers the PhysioNet statement over the project documentation and says why; on participant counts it prefers the PhysioNet per-feature figures; on the enrolment target it prefers the more recent 10,000 over the 30,000 in the IRB protocol and white paper; on two investigator names it prefers the PhysioNet spellings.

Temporal values are internally consistent where they can be checked: issued 2026-05-01 matches the 1 May 2026 release of version 3.1.0 in distribution_dates, the version slot matches the version-pinned landing page, and the funded project period to 30 November 2026 postdates the release.

The limitations disclosure includes the consortium's own AI-readiness self-assessment failures (data quality under characterisation, domain-appropriate and associated criteria under sustainability, contextualised under computability), which is a record reporting the scores it did not achieve alongside the seven categories where it reports 100 percent.

correctness_validations.doi_format: valid (10.13026/8xbn-nq66 in id and doi, 10.13026/37yb-1t42 as the latest-version DOI, and 10.13026/249v-w155, 10.13026/k81f-qr68, 10.13026/h995-bt35 and 10.13026/mf9s-5r03 elsewhere all carry the PhysioNet prefix; 10.57764/qb6h-em84 is attributed to the Health Data Nexus and 10.5281/zenodo.12760724 and 10.5281/zenodo.13834653 to Zenodo, both prefixes matching their stated registrars)
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: valid (OT2OD032720 matches the NIH activity-code and institute pattern for an Other Transaction award from the Office of the Director, and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 is a well-formed full award number with a supplement suffix; source_caveats records four further renderings found in the sources, including the malformed '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2', and states that the core project number was preferred)
correctness_validations.rrid_format: valid_in_prose (RRID:SCR_007345 matches the RRID:SCR_ pattern and is the correct identifier for PhysioNet, but it sits inside the citation string rather than an identifier slot, and it identifies the hosting platform rather than the dataset)
correctness_validations.url_validity: all_well_formed (the version-pinned PhysioNet landing page, the Synapse controlled-access endpoint syn72370534, four GitHub repositories, two Zenodo archives, docs.b2ai-voice.org and the Scholars programme page are all well formed and plausible for the organisations named; the FHIR profiles entry names a resource without a URL and says so explicitly rather than inventing one)

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42; citation carries RRID:SCR_007345
sub_elements.quality_note: Well-formed DOI whose 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's registrar prefix, matching the landing page, the citation and the hosting platform named in maintainers. The id is a CURIE rather than a resolver URL, consistent with the schema's identifier form, and the record separates the version-specific DOI it is identified by from the version-agnostic DOI that resolves to the latest release.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description of roughly 1,800 characters naming the five disease cohort categories, the recruitment setting, the four-part participant protocol, the 833 participants across five North American sites, the derived features in the public release, the exclusion of raw audio, and the consortium's AI-readiness self-assessment scores
sub_elements.quality_note: Far above the 200-character threshold and specific throughout. It states what the public release contains and, unusually, what it does not: the original recordings are withheld and disseminated only under controlled access. Every modality and cohort it names reappears in a structured slot later in the record.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice]
sub_elements.quality_note: Four keywords against a threshold of five, and all four are single generic words. The record itself names five disease cohort categories, eight derived feature families, BIDS, REDCap, ICD-10, PhysioNet and Synapse, none of which reach the keyword set. This is the record's one clear discovery failure: a search for speech, cough, spectrogram, MFCC, dysphonia or machine learning would not surface it on keywords.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; distribution_formats[].access_urls carry the same landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ for the controlled-access audio
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable, version-pinned landing page on a recognised repository, matching the version slot exactly, with a second access endpoint for the restricted tier. The sub-element is satisfied by the landing page alone; no hierarchical resources or file_collections structure is carried, so a user cannot see the file inventory, sizes or checksums from this record.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: two entries, relationship_type is_supplemented_by targeting doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 (Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset, with its own version, counts and latest-version DOI) and is_new_version_of targeting doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 (the version 1.0 Health Data Nexus release)
sub_elements.quality_note: Two typed relationships, each with a target DOI, a name and a description of what the related release contains. The pediatric companion is correctly held at arm's length as a related dataset rather than absorbed into this one, and the record states that decision in source_caveats.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; license_terms describing the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, the credentialing and signature requirement, permitted duplication, the prohibition on sale, and the Fort Lauderdale Agreement; ip_restrictions.restrictions setting out copyright, the absence of any transfer of rights, and downstream IP subject to non-obstructive licensing
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves are substantive. The IP paragraph does the harder work: it states that the provider gives no guarantee the data are free of third-party rights, that no rights transfer to the recipient, and that recipients may hold rights on downstream discoveries only under licensing policies that will not obstruct further research.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions: 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply'; other_compliance describing the Certificate of Confidentiality, the safeguards recipients must apply, and a five-business-day breach reporting obligation
sub_elements.quality_note: All four fields the sub-element names are populated, and the negative claim about export controls is stated rather than left blank. The breach-reporting window and the certificate's application against subpoenas are operational detail a recipient can act on.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[].access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; data_governance.access_review_process describing PhysioNet registration, identity confirmation and agreement signature for the feature release, and the Data Access Request Form, Data Use Agreement, DACO review and institutionally signed DTUA for the raw audio; contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org
sub_elements.quality_note: No download_url slot is populated, and the record says three times why: 'No direct download URL is published: the PhysioNet files are gated behind credentialing and a signed data use agreement.' The sub-element admits platform access instructions in place of a direct link, and the instructions here are complete enough to execute, including the separate route and contact address for the restricted tier.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: three entries naming Apache Parquet for the dense derived features with a per-recording metadata file, tab-separated values with accompanying JSON data dictionaries for the static features, quality metrics and six phenotype tables, and WAV with JSON sidecars organised under BIDS participant and session directories for the controlled-access audio
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are named specifically and each is tied to the content it carries and the access tier it sits behind, so a reuser can tell before applying which tier holds the data they need. No MIME types or media_type values are given, and no file sizes or counts, which is the remaining gap.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: two typed entries with target DOIs; external_resources: six entries covering eipm/bridge2ai-redcap with its Zenodo archive, sensein/b2aiprep, sensein/senselab, eipm/bridge2ai-docs with its Zenodo archive and the docs.b2ai-voice.org site, the consortium FHIR profiles, and the Bridge2AI-Voice Scholars training programme
sub_elements.quality_note: Four of the six external resources carry a repository URL, two carry a Zenodo archival DOI and an archival flag, and three carry a licence. The FHIR profiles entry names the resource and states plainly that the captured text gives no repository URL, which is a declared gap rather than a fabricated link.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: license: Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; intended_uses.usage_notes: 'intended solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers who have been approved and have signed the applicable access agreement'; 'There are no fees associated with these restrictions'
sub_elements.quality_note: Not a standard Creative Commons instrument, but the permissions are stated explicitly and permissively for research: both commercial and non-commercial research are allowed, there are no fees, duplication for the approved project is permitted, and the record commits to licensing policies that will not obstruct further research. The gating is credentialing, not a use restriction on approved researchers.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats naming Apache Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented data file format'), tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries, and WAV with JSON sidecars; conforms_to: Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0
sub_elements.quality_note: Every format is open and tool-independent, and the audio tier is laid out under a named, versioned community standard rather than a bespoke directory scheme. Character encoding is not stated for the TSV tier, which is the one omission the sub-element's field list asks for.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:25 and B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; labeling_strategies: 'Labels follow the Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes'
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted at four levels: the data organisation standard with a version, the metadata schema by persistent URI, the ontology CURIEs on the instance entries, and the clinical coding system behind the diagnostic labels. preprocessing_strategies corroborates the BIDS claim by describing the conversion path, including the pediatric ReproSchema to REDCap to BIDS route.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: participant_id and session_id, each data_type identifier with is_identifier true and a note describing its role ('present in every Parquet feature file and used to join the phenotype tables'; 'a participant may have more than one session'), plus task_name (categorical) and n_frames (integer)
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on the sub-element's own purpose, which is integration: the join keys are named, typed, flagged as identifiers and described in terms of how they link the Parquet features to the phenotype tables, and relationships states that a participant may hold several sessions. That is what a reuser needs to merge these tables with another source. The set is nonetheless only four entries; the composition consequence is scored at Element 5 sub-element 3.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: two use categories with examples and usage notes; prohibited_uses: five prohibitions covering re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatisation, obstructive IP claims, sale of the data, and contacting subjects without IRB approval and provider consent; discouraged_uses: two, covering hiring, insurance and surveillance applications and uses that ignore the dataset's skews; existing_uses and future_use_impacts also populated
sub_elements.quality_note: The strongest use guidance in the record. The prohibitions are specific and enforceable rather than generic, each tied to the agreement that imposes it, and the discouraged uses name concrete downstream harms. future_use_impacts adds the consortium's own view of voice AI risks, including voice re-identification and voice AI hacking.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects: met on fields outside Element 4. E1 description states 'Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics at academic institutions in the United States and Canada on the basis of membership in five disease cohort categories' and reports 'data for 833 participants across five North American sites'. E8 collection_mechanisms describe a tablet application administered in clinic, reproschema-ui for the pediatric protocol, REDCap questionnaire capture and named recording hardware, all of which are participant-facing. E2 regulatory_restrictions carries confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant' and a Certificate of Confidentiality under other_compliance. Element 4's own fields were not used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: true; irb_approval: approval by the University of South Florida IRB with subsites engaged through the single IRB process; ethics_review_board naming USF as single IRB, the SickKids Research Ethics Board for the pediatric cohort and separate Canadian REB approvals; ethical_reviews: three entries including a Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group that 'identified the sensitive fields removed from the release and produced a memorandum setting out the ethical justification for controlled access to raw voice data samples'; data_governance.committee_name: Bridge2AI-Voice Data Access Compliance Office (DACO) with contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org
sub_elements.quality_note: The consistency expectation triggered by involves_human_subjects is met at full strength: named boards, the multi-jurisdiction structure, and a governance committee with a contact route. No formal data protection impact assessment is named as such, but the ethics working group's field-by-field sensitivity determination and its published memorandum on controlled access do the equivalent work and are traceable.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects: met on fields outside Element 4. E1 description states 'Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics at academic institutions in the United States and Canada on the basis of membership in five disease cohort categories' and reports 'data for 833 participants across five North American sites'. E8 collection_mechanisms describe a tablet application administered in clinic, reproschema-ui for the pediatric protocol, REDCap questionnaire capture and named recording hardware, all of which are participant-facing. E2 regulatory_restrictions carries confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant' and a Certificate of Confidentiality under other_compliance. Element 4's own fields were not used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of non-identifying but highly sensitive fields, and by exclusion of the raw audio'; identifiers_removed enumerating the Safe Harbor set plus state and province, household composition and cultural identity, and sensitive fields such as household income and mental health status; deidentification_details: dates rebased to integers, geography generalised, narrative text removed, transcripts reviewed and recordings containing identifying information or external voices removed
sub_elements.quality_note: A named method with the identifier set enumerated rather than gestured at, and the method is appropriate for the data type: Safe Harbor alone does not address voice, so the record supplements it by withholding the waveform and by reviewing transcripts for identifying content. It also concedes what the method does not achieve, stating that k-anonymisation with k of 2 or more is not reached.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects: met on fields outside Element 4. E1 description states 'Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics at academic institutions in the United States and Canada on the basis of membership in five disease cohort categories' and reports 'data for 833 participants across five North American sites'. E8 collection_mechanisms describe a tablet application administered in clinic, reproschema-ui for the pediatric protocol, REDCap questionnaire capture and named recording hardware, all of which are participant-facing. E2 regulatory_restrictions carries confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant' and a Certificate of Confidentiality under other_compliance. Element 4's own fields were not used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method, privacy_techniques describing 'a two-tier access model - registered or credentialed access for the feature-only data and controlled access for the raw audio', reidentification_risk: 'each person's voice is unique to them and re-identification by voice cannot be entirely excluded, which is the reason raw audio is disseminated only under controlled access', and data_linkage: internal study numbers with the linking tables held behind institutional access controls and not shared between sites
sub_elements.quality_note: The risk assessment is explicit, negative where the evidence is negative, and load-bearing: the stated risk is what justifies the access architecture rather than being recorded beside it. data_linkage closes the loop by saying where the re-identification key lives and who holds it.

E8 collection_mechanisms describe a tablet application administered in clinic, reproschema-ui for the pediatric protocol, REDCap questionnaire capture and named recording hardware, all of which are participant-facing. E2 regulatory_restrictions carries confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant' and a Certificate of Confidentiality under other_compliance. Element 4's own fields were not used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type covering paper signature, electronic consent in the application or a REDCap survey, and a video consent in which the participant reads a statement aloud so the acoustic data can be verified as belonging to the consented individual; consent_scope covering collection, sharing without direct identifiers, registered access release and controlled access release, and EHR access for gold standard validation; consent_documentation with a five-year minimum retention and re-consent before each subsequent collection; withdrawal_mechanism; plus collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations
sub_elements.quality_note: The consent scope maps one-to-one onto the two-tier release the record actually describes, so the distribution model is covered by what participants agreed to rather than merely compatible with it. The withdrawal terms are stated honestly, including the limit that data contributed before withdrawal are retained once collection is complete.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects: met on fields outside Element 4. E1 description states 'Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics at academic institutions in the United States and Canada on the basis of membership in five disease cohort categories' and reports 'data for 833 participants across five North American sites'. E8 collection_mechanisms describe a tablet application administered in clinic, reproschema-ui for the pediatric protocol, REDCap questionnaire capture and named recording hardware, all of which are participant-facing. E2 regulatory_restrictions carries confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant' and a Certificate of Confidentiality under other_compliance. Element 4's own fields were not used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true with special_protections for participants with cognitive impairment, dementia and psychiatric conditions and for pediatric participants, including a comprehension check in which 'potential participants are asked to explain what they have understood'; guardian_consent and assent_procedures including the under-seven exception; participant_compensation: electronic gift cards, 40 US dollars under 90 minutes and 80 over, capped at three sessions and 120 dollars total, adults only, with a source caveat that the earlier feasibility study paid nothing
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves are concrete. The compensation figures are exact, with the cap and the adult-only restriction stated, which is the detail an ethics reviewer would ask for on undue inducement. The teach-back comprehension check and the documented assent practice are protections specific to the populations named rather than boilerplate.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: two entries, the first identifying demographic subpopulations by age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status in the demographics table with a distribution note on skews by disorder category and site, the second identifying the five disease cohort categories plus controls with a note that the releases do not contain an equal distribution and that the initial release covered four of the five; sampling_strategies.strategies describing recruitment at high-volume expert clinics against predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the demographic and the clinical axes are described, each with an identification route into a named table and a distribution statement that is candid about imbalance. The note that groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI were less likely to be recruited is a mechanism, not just an observation of skew.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances[0]: instance_type research participant, counts 833; description: 'Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 participants across five North American sites'; source_caveats giving the per-feature recording counts for version 3.1.0 (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms, 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram files) against approximately 61,937 voice-derived recordings reported for version 3.0 in the project documentation
sub_elements.quality_note: A specific participant count in the structured slot, corroborated in the description and attributed to a named release. The recording-level counts exist and are attributed to the higher-ranked source, but they sit in trailing prose while the audio recording instance entry carries no counts, so a structured consumer sees only the participant figure. splits records that no recommended splits are provided, which is an answer rather than a gap.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: variables: four entries only (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames); no is_tabular flag anywhere in the record; the phenotype tier is described only at group level, as 'the phenotype tables covering confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires and task metadata'
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on this sub-element's own purpose, which is whether the dataset's structure can be understood from the metadata. Four variables, three of them keys and one a frame count, do not describe six phenotype tables and a set of dense feature files. No column is documented for demographics, diagnosis, enrolment or the validated questionnaires, no value sets or units are given, and the is_tabular flag the sub-element names is absent. The record does say that JSON data dictionaries ship alongside the TSV files, so the information exists in the distribution; it is not in the datasheet, and a reuser cannot size or interpret the tables before applying for access. The join keys that are documented are credited at Element 3 sub-element 4.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances carry data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:25 and B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; label_description enumerating the disease cohort categories as voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, or control; labeling_strategies tying labels to ICD-10 codes; description naming pediatric voice and speech disorders as the fifth category
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are expressed twice over: as ontology CURIEs on the instance entries and as named clinical cohorts in prose, with ICD-10 as the coding system behind the labels. The modalities covered (voice, speech, breathing, cough) are stated consistently in the description, acquisition_methods and preprocessing_strategies.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: three entries covering differing site collection configurations and a protocol that changed during the study, recording noise artifacts and diagnostic practice variation between sites and clinicians, and audio files that could not generate certain features and are therefore absent from the Parquet files; sampling_strategies with is_random false, is_representative false and a why_not_representative statement; missing_data_documentation with causes, patterns and handling
sub_elements.quality_note: The three fields the sub-element names are all populated and mutually reinforcing. missing_data_documentation is the strongest part: it explains the one-row-per-visit structure that produces repeated participant rows with possibly differing responses, reports that a missingness table ships with the release, and states that no imputation is applied, which is exactly what a modeller needs before joining the tables.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Version 2.0.0 reprocessed the spectrograms and removed all spectrograms and MFCCs derived from free speech recordings; version 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list; version 3.1.0 'fixed broken Parquet files carried in the version 3.0.0 release, and back-filled and updated validated diagnosis information across conditions; some phenotype files were rearranged and certain gold standard variable names were renamed'

The 3.1.0 entry is the one that matters most to a reuser holding 3.0.0: broken files, changed diagnosis values and renamed variables are all break-your-pipeline changes, and all three are disclosed.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. sub_elements.quality_note: A stated cadence, the reasons a new version is cut, and the notification route. The stated frequency understates the observed one: distribution_dates shows six releases in roughly eighteen months, which is nearer quarterly, and that tension is logged as a low-severity accuracy issue rather than scored against this sub-element.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: two entries, the WAV waveforms captured with the Bridge2AI-Voice application with source_type 'primary prospective collection' and access_details naming the Synapse route, and the REDCap and ReproSchema-UI study records with their export format and release tier; preprocessing_strategies tracing waveform to feature; distribution_dates with the full release history; related_datasets is_new_version_of the Health Data Nexus release
sub_elements.quality_note: The derivation chain is complete in both directions: where the raw data came from, how each released feature family was computed from it, which release this supersedes, and where the raw tier can still be requested. No was_derived_from or release_notes slot is used, but the substance those slots would carry is present and attributed.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: five responses covering generation of a diverse voice dataset linked to multimodal health biomarkers, development and validation of clinically applicable models, integration of voice as a biomarker in clinical care, new standards for acoustic data collection and analysis, and audiomics storage and sharing infrastructure with ethical and legal norms; addressing_gaps: four responses naming small sample sizes and missing metadata in prior work, the size, quality and diversity limits of open voice datasets against private industry holdings, the absence of measurement standards that prevents pooling, and the sparse pediatric literature
sub_elements.quality_note: Motivation is given twice over, as forward-looking purposes and as the specific deficiencies in the prior art that each purpose answers. The addressing_gaps entries are the stronger half because they are falsifiable claims about the field rather than aspirations.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: three responses covering disease detection and classification from voice, speech, breathing and cough recordings with labels spanning the four adult cohort categories, pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking or validation of models on voice data, and screening, diagnosis and monitoring using voice as a non-invasive biomarker
sub_elements.quality_note: The tasks are machine-learning-specific and each names the label space or the model lifecycle stage it applies to, so a reuser can tell which of the released feature families supports which task. They align with the intended_uses categories rather than restating the purposes.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund', with notes recording that 'The funded project period runs from 1 September 2022 to 30 November 2026, with the project administered by the University of South Florida'; description attributing the work to 'the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program'
sub_elements.quality_note: The funding agency, the specific funding mechanism within it, the administering institution and the project period are all recorded. The stated purposes match what the Common Fund Bridge2AI programme funds, so the funding logic check passes.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders.grants: OT2OD032720 and 3OT2OD032720-01S1; source_caveats: 'Grant identifier renderings vary across the sources: OT2OD032720 as the core project number, 3OT2OD032720-01S1 in the dataset acknowledgements, 3OT2OD032720-01S3 as the NIH RePORTER application, 1OT2OD032720-01 in the feasibility publication, and "3Tf-OTOD03272001S2" in the documentation footer'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both recorded identifiers match NIH patterns: OT2 as the Other Transaction activity code, OD as the Office of the Director, a six-digit serial, and in the second a type prefix with a supplement suffix. The record goes further than the sub-element asks by listing the competing renderings it found and declining the malformed footer string, which is the correct handling of a source conflict on an identifier.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: created_by: Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium; creators: fifteen named individuals, each with an institutional affiliation spanning USF, Weill Cornell, Vanderbilt, SickKids, WashU, OHSU, Simon Fraser, The Hastings Center, MIT, Toronto, Sinai Health and Florida; citation carrying the full PhysioNet author list; maintainers and data_governance.accountable_organization naming the institutions responsible
sub_elements.quality_note: Coverage is good and every creator carries an affiliation, so institutional accountability is traceable. The role typing is wrong, however: all fifteen are typed principal_investigator while the record's own notes identify only Bensoussan and Elemento as co-PIs, which is logged as a medium-severity correctness issue. No ORCIDs are recorded for any creator.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified and datasets shared: both met. acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms are populated with four entries each, direct_collection records is_direct true, and data_collectors names who administered the protocol. The shared condition holds as set out for Element 3.
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: four entries covering the custom Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application hosting the acoustic protocol and surveys, reproschema-ui for the pediatric protocol, REDCap capture and export for questionnaire and clinical validation data, and the recording hardware ('iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; a head-mounted headset with microphone was used where possible'); collection_timeframes, data_collectors and direct_collection also populated
sub_elements.quality_note: The hardware entry is the standout: specific device generations, a named microphone model, the connection path, and the admission that 'the microphone could sit at slightly different distances between recordings', which is a measurement confound disclosed at the point it arises and carried through to known_biases. The clinical setting, the collectors and the pediatric variant are all described.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 1: collection is identified on acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms and raw_data_sources, and the dataset is shared.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: four typed entries with was_directly_observed for the prospectively captured recordings, was_reported_by_subjects for demographics, medical history, confounders and validated questionnaires, was_validated_verified for clinician diagnoses confirmed against audio, imaging, electronic health records or prescriptions, and was_inferred_derived for the released acoustic features; raw_data_sources: two entries with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details
sub_elements.quality_note: All four acquisition modes are typed correctly against what they describe, and the distinction that matters most for this release is drawn explicitly: the public payload is inferred and derived, not directly observed. The validation entry names the gold standard route per cohort rather than asserting clinical confirmation generically.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software tools produced as dataset output: met on fields outside Element 8. E10 external_resources references four code repositories - sensein/b2aiprep 'the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset', sensein/senselab, eipm/bridge2ai-redcap and eipm/bridge2ai-docs - two of them with Zenodo archival DOIs and three with licences. E7 purposes also identify infrastructure and standards development as project outputs. Element 8's own fields were not used to reach this determination.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: eight entries with parameters, including 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter, spectrograms from a short-time FFT with 25 ms window, 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT then downsampled by two in time, sixty MFCCs and 60-bin Mel spectrograms, sparc articulatory traces at 50 Hz, openSMILE, Parselmouth and Praat features, ppgs posteriorgrams over 40 acoustic units at 100 Hz, Whisper Large transcription, and BIDS v1.9.0 conversion; cleaning_strategies: an audit protocol generating missingness tables, checking distributions, outliers and categorical responses against the schema, and running audio QC on silence and duration and comparing produced speech against the intended passage; labeling_strategies with annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_protocol and data_annotation_platform; machine_annotation_tools recording Whisper with the caveat that off-the-shelf models 'have not been audited for correctness'
sub_elements.quality_note: The most technically transparent part of the record. Every released feature family can be traced to the tool and the numeric parameters that produced it, so the Parquet columns are interpretable. The labeling side is equally candid: one annotator per item, the annotator identified as the site clinician or a prior external clinician, the protocol tied to ICD-10, and the platform named. The unaudited-transcription caveat is carried into known_limitations rather than left as a footnote.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 3: E10 external_resources references four code repositories with URLs, two with Zenodo archival DOIs, and E7 purposes identify infrastructure development as a project output.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources naming sensein/b2aiprep at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep under Apache-2.0 as 'the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset, convert the raw audio waveforms into the Parquet feature files and merge the source data into the phenotype files', sensein/senselab, eipm/bridge2ai-redcap with a Zenodo archive under MIT, and eipm/bridge2ai-docs with a Zenodo archive; preprocessing_strategies naming sparc, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat and ppgs; machine_annotation_tools naming OpenAI Whisper Large; extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep
sub_elements.quality_note: The tools are named, the production pipeline is attributed to a specific open-source library with a resolvable repository and a licence, and a contribution route is given. Two gaps keep this from being complete: there is no software_and_tools slot, so the information is scattered across three other slots, and no library carries a version except Whisper Large and BIDS v1.9.0. Since openSMILE and Praat feature values are version-dependent, the released features cannot be regenerated exactly from what is recorded. Both are logged as a medium-severity correctness issue.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; external_resources: six entries including the REDCap data dictionary and instrument PDFs archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724, the documentation site https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, the consortium FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, and the Bridge2AI-Voice Scholars programme at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/; labeling_strategies referencing ICD-10
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards are referenced at the data organisation, clinical coding, interoperability and metadata schema levels, and two of the supporting resources carry archival DOIs rather than bare repository links, so they remain citable if the repositories move. The FHIR entry declares that the captured text gives no repository URL instead of supplying one.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries covering representativeness with a recommended mitigation, coverage (English only, Spanish protocols still under development), temporal (distribution shift from changing diagnostic criteria), scope (derived features rather than recordings, with spectrogram-family features and free-speech transcripts additionally excluded, and a scope_impact stating that tasks needing the waveform require controlled access), and two methodological entries covering the single labeler and the consortium's own unmet AI-readiness criteria
sub_elements.quality_note: Each limitation carries a type, and three carry a mitigation or an impact statement, so the section tells a reuser what to do about the limitation rather than only that it exists. The scope entry is the most useful: it states precisely which analyses the registered-access release cannot support. Reporting the consortium's own failed self-assessment criteria is voluntary disclosure against interest.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: four entries with distinct schema enum values. representation_bias (five sites in two countries, fluent English speakers only) with a mitigation_strategy of remote collection and Spanish expansion; selection_bias (groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI, or less proximal to sites, less likely to be recruited); measurement_bias (screening by site means disease groups were recorded on different devices and configurations) with affected_subsets; annotation_bias (single labeler per instance, differing diagnostic basis by cohort); future_use_impacts adding downstream fairness and voice AI risk statements
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct taxonomy values, each grounded in a specific collection fact rather than a generic caution, with mitigation where mitigation exists and affected subsets where the bias is localised. The measurement bias entry is the one that would most affect a classifier, because it means device identity is confounded with disease cohort, and the record states that confound plainly.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: three entries covering differing site collection configurations and a protocol that changed over the study, sources of noise and error including recording artifacts, diagnostic practice variation, inaccurate questionnaire responses and underreporting, and audio files that could not generate certain features and are therefore missing from the corresponding Parquet feature files
sub_elements.quality_note: The third entry is operationally important and consistent with missing_data_documentation: a reuser joining Parquet feature files will find recordings present in one feature family and absent from another, and the record says so in advance. Underreporting and inaccurate self-report are named rather than assumed away.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: content_warnings.content_warnings_present: true, warning that free speech tasks mean offensive, insulting or threatening content 'cannot be completely avoided because research participants are responsible for their choice of language', with the mitigation that free-speech transcripts and spectrogram-family features from free speech were removed, and a source_caveats reconciling the project documentation against the PhysioNet statement in favour of the more recent source; sensitive_elements: four entries covering race and ethnic origin, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information, and the re-identification potential of raw voice
sub_elements.quality_note: Both fields are populated and the content warning states the residual risk, the reason it cannot be eliminated, and the specific step taken to reduce it in this release. The source caveat shows the ranking rule being applied to a live disagreement between two sources about what the release contains, which is exactly where a reader needs it.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: three entries. The USF IRB reviewed and approved the acquisition protocol and the sharing of the resulting data, with United States sites brought under the same approval; the SickKids Research Ethics Board approved collection and sharing for the pediatric cohort; a Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group 'identified the sensitive fields removed from the release and produced a memorandum setting out the ethical justification for controlled access to raw voice data samples, which is published alongside the dataset documentation'
sub_elements.quality_note: Three reviewing bodies with substantive, differentiated descriptions of what each reviewed, and the working group entry documents a review that produced a published, checkable artifact. Conflicts of interest are the missing half: no competing interest, commercial relationship or industry involvement is recorded anywhere in the record.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; citation ending 'PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345'; maintainers: 'PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, hosts the current dataset versions and administers credentialed access' and the Health Data Nexus at T-CAIREM, University of Toronto for the earlier release; third_party_sharing: 'through the PhysioNet data publishing platform under registered and credentialed access, and through Synapse for the raw audio'
sub_elements.quality_note: Three recognised platforms are identified with their roles distinguished: PhysioNet for the current feature releases, Synapse for the controlled-access audio, and the Health Data Nexus for the superseded release. No publisher slot is populated, so the platform is readable by a person but not by a harvester reading that field, which is logged as a medium-severity consistency issue.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified and datasets shared: both met. citation carries a complete formatted reference with author list, year, title, version, publisher, RRID and resolvable DOI URL, and external_resources adds two Zenodo-archived supporting publications. The shared condition holds as set out for Element 3.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., Powell, M., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; version_access.version_details listing the per-version DOIs
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, copy-ready citation carrying author list, year, versioned title, publisher, resource identifier and a resolvable DOI URL, and the DOI in the citation matches the doi and id slots exactly. Version-specific DOIs elsewhere mean a downstream paper can cite the exact release it used.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared and available for reuse: met. distribution_formats carries three entries (Apache Parquet features, tab-separated phenotype tables with JSON data dictionaries, WAV audio under BIDS); page resolves to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use and the license terms permit commercial and non-commercial research by approved users. Gating behind credentialing does not unset the condition; under the ambiguity rule a partially shared dataset is scored on what is documented.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; external_resources naming the Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker; labeling_strategies referencing ICD-10; instances carrying B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE CURIEs
sub_elements.quality_note: Four independent community standards are named: BIDS with a version for data organisation, FHIR for clinical interoperability, ICD-10 for diagnostic coding, and the Bridge2AI data sheets schema by persistent URI for the metadata itself. Applying BIDS to voice is an uncommon choice and the record documents the conversion path that makes the claim checkable.

sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_supplemented_by targeting doi:10.13026/h995-bt35, the Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset, described with its separate REB approval, its version 1.1.0 content of 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2 to 18, and its latest-version DOI 10.13026/mf9s-5r03; relationship_type is_new_version_of targeting doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84, the version 1.0 Health Data Nexus release
sub_elements.quality_note: Both relationships are typed with vocabulary terms, both targets are DOIs rather than names, and both descriptions say what the related release contains and why it is separate. Holding the pediatric dataset as related rather than absorbing it into this record is the correct scope decision, and the record states it explicitly in source_caveats.

strengths: Ethics documentation is complete across all five Element 4 sub-elements and internally consistent: named IRBs in two jurisdictions, an ethics working group whose sensitivity determination produced a published memorandum, HIPAA Safe Harbor supplemented for the voice-specific risk, consent whose stated scope maps onto the two access tiers actually operated, and exact compensation figures with a stated cap.

The re-identification assessment is load-bearing rather than decorative. It concedes that k-anonymisation with k of 2 or more is not achieved and that a voice is unique to its speaker, and the two-tier access architecture is derived from that finding, which is why the waveforms are withheld from the registered-access release.

Processing is documented at parameter level: 16 kHz monaural resampling with an anti-aliasing filter, a 25 ms window with 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT, sixty MFCCs, articulatory traces at 50 Hz and posteriorgrams over 40 units at 100 Hz. Every released feature family can be traced to the tool and the numbers that produced it.

Version and provenance tracking is unusually complete: six releases enumerated with hosts and dates, version-specific DOIs distinguished from the latest-version DOI, per-version errata that disclose broken files and renamed variables, a stated update cadence and a notification route.

Bias documentation uses four distinct taxonomy values, each grounded in a specific collection fact with mitigation or affected subsets where they apply, and the measurement bias entry names the device-by-cohort confound that would most affect a downstream classifier.

Source conflicts are surfaced and adjudicated rather than smoothed over. The record ranks sources explicitly on the free-speech transcripts, the recording counts, the enrolment target, the collection window and two investigator name spellings, and it declines a malformed grant identifier found in a documentation footer.
weaknesses: keywords carries four generic single words against a record naming five disease cohorts, eight derived feature families, four modalities, BIDS, REDCap, ICD-10, PhysioNet and Synapse. This is the record's one outright scoring failure on discovery and the easiest to fix.

Variable-level metadata covers four entries, three of them keys, against six phenotype tables and several dense feature families. No column is documented for demographics, diagnosis, enrolment or the validated questionnaires, no value sets or units are given, and no is_tabular flag is set, so the table structure cannot be understood before applying for access.

No software_and_tools slot exists and no feature-extraction library carries a version. openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, sparc, ppgs, b2aiprep and senselab are named without version or release tag, so the released Parquet features cannot be regenerated exactly from what is recorded.

No publisher slot is populated. PhysioNet is unambiguous to a human reader from the page, citation, maintainers and third_party_sharing, but a metadata harvester reading the publisher field gets nothing from the most-cited slot in the sub-element.

All fifteen creators are typed principal_investigator while the record's own notes identify only two as co-PIs, so thirteen entries assert a role the record does not evidence. No creator carries an ORCID.

Two smaller gaps close the loop: conflicts of interest are absent from ethical_reviews, and the recording-level counts sit in trailing source_caveats prose rather than in the audio recording instance entry, leaving 833 participants as the only structured count.
recommendations: Expand keywords to at least a dozen terms drawn from the record's own content, covering modality (speech, cough, breathing), derived feature family (spectrogram, MFCC, phonetic posteriorgram), disease cohort, standard (BIDS, ICD-10) and hosting platform (PhysioNet, Synapse).

Document the phenotype tables at column level, or at minimum the demographics and diagnosis tables, with data types, value sets and units, and set is_tabular so the structure is machine-readable without applying for access.

Add a software_and_tools entry for each tool in the pipeline, pinning b2aiprep, senselab, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, sparc and ppgs to the versions or release tags used for this release, since feature values depend on them.
Populate publisher with PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, matching the platform already named in the citation, maintainers and third_party_sharing.
Re-type creators so that principal_investigator applies only to the two contributors the sources name as co-PIs, and record ORCIDs where the sources give them.

Reconcile sensitive_elements with is_deidentified by naming the demographic variables retained in the released phenotype tables, and state whether the Certificate of Confidentiality attaches to the released features or only to the identifiable source data held at sites.

Move the per-feature recording counts from source_caveats into the audio recording instance entry, keeping the caveat that the sources disagree on a single recording total, and record conflicts of interest in ethical_reviews even if the declaration is nil.
